platform_notes: Genius POS is Global Payments' Genius for Restaurants software (formerly Heartland Restaurant) on GC26/XC23 countertop stations, Mobile 2.0 handhelds or iPads, managed through a web Admin Portal; Global Payments publishes a large help centre for it. Paradise POS is an iPad/Android POS app whose own manual covers PAX and Castles card terminals, Epson printers and its cloud dashboard. Our sheets say the Basil bundles run Basil software on Dejavoo P18/P8 terminals on the Paradise platform, but nothing on paradisepos.com mentions Basil or Dejavoo, so no entry here is tagged to the Basil devices. HotSauce POS is a Windows-based, non-cloud restaurant system sold through resellers.

entries.title: Set up the Titan 3000 cellular router
steps: Run an Ethernet cord from your modem to the WAN port of the cellular router.
Plug the router into a power outlet with the included adapter and turn on the power switch.
Wait for the SYS light to change from orange to green, which means startup has finished.
The router connects to the strongest available signal by itself.
Use the remaining LAN ports to connect switches that run the network to your stations.
entries.quote: The device’s SYS LED indicator will change from

entries.title: Set up the Plasma Cloud PA2200 access point
steps: Find the PoE injector, a small rectangular box with a power port and two Ethernet ports.
Run an Ethernet cord from your router or modem to the LAN port of the PoE injector.
Run a second Ethernet cord from the PoE port of the injector to the port marked 54V PoE - Ethernet 2 on the access point.
Plug the power cord into the PoE injector. The injector powers the access point.
entries.quote: Connect the power cord to the PoE injector, which will supply power to the access point.

steps: Connect an Ethernet cord to the 10/100Base-TX port on the printer and connect the power cord.
Open the paper tray and load kitchen printer paper following the instructions inside the tray.
Turn the printer on with the power toggle switch and wait for a green light.
Within about a minute the printer should print a short settings page. Keep it: it shows the MAC address and IP address.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance and pick the kitchen printer in the list on the left, or create a new one.
Name the printer, select Printer Model and choose Epson Thermal.
Select the scan button and pick the MAC address that matches your printed slip, or type the IP address in by hand.
Select Save, then select Test Print. A test slip should print.

Connect an Ethernet cord to the Ethernet port.
If you use a cash drawer, plug the end of the drawer cord labeled Printer into the printer's Cash Drawer port.

Connect the power cord to the 24V power port, decide whether paper loads from the top or the front, and put the plates back with the rubber-bumper plate on the base.

Connect the USB cord from the Paradise device to the port labeled iPad 2.1A on the back of the printer.
If you use a cash drawer, plug the end of the drawer cord labeled Printer into the printer's Cash Drawer port.

Remove the back cover of the terminal and plug the communication cable into the Type-C port.

Select WiFi, choose your network, enter the Wi-Fi password and confirm. It must be the same network the Paradise station is on.

Unhook the latch to make room for the cords.
Run an Ethernet cord from your router to the Ethernet port.
Plug the supplied power cable into a wall outlet and then into the device, and close the latch over the cords.

entries.quote: Flip the Castles V3000 device with the screen facing

steps: Plug the scanner's USB cord into the port labeled USB on the back of your receipt printer.
Connect the printer following the instructions for that printer.
Open the Paradise app and log in.
Scan a barcode. The app should either ring up the item or prompt you to create a new item. If it does, the scanner is connected.
entries.quote: This scanner will connect to the USB port on the back

steps: Make sure the scanner is turned on, in range and fully charged. It should already be paired when you receive it.
On the Paradise device, open the Settings app and open Bluetooth settings.
Make sure Bluetooth is turned on and connected to the scanner.
If the scanner is not connected, select it in the list to connect it.
Open the Paradise app, log in and scan a barcode. The app should ring up the item or prompt you to create a new item.

entries.title: Connect a Paradise station by cable with the hardwire kit
steps: Connect the USB power cord to the USB port on the hardwire kit.
Run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the Ethernet port on the hardwire kit.
Connect the power cord on the hardwire kit to the Paradise device.
Open the Settings app on the Paradise device and turn Wi-Fi off.
If the device shows a separate Ethernet section, the hardwire kit is connected properly.
entries.quote: Make sure Wi-Fi is turned off. Your device should have a separate Ethernet section.

entries.title: Set up the Paradise kitchen display (KDS) tablet
steps: Ethernet model: run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the tablet's Ethernet port. Wi-Fi model: attach the Wi-Fi antenna if it is not already attached.
Connect power and turn on the device.
Open the Google browser. It should already be on the right page; if not, go to paradiseposkds.com.
The device should connect to your database automatically.
If it shows a setup screen instead, contact Paradise support to schedule your installation.
entries.quote: page, if not, navigate to paradiseposkds.com.

entries.title: Connect and test the KB9000 bump bar
steps: Plug the bump bar into either USB port on the KDS tablet.
On the KDS, use the arrows to change the highlighted ticket, or use the bump bar buttons to bump a test ticket.
entries.quote: The bump bar connects to the tablet via USB.

entries.title: Set up the Star MG-T60 scale
steps: Plug the scale into power and turn it on.
The scale should already be connected to the Paradise device.
To test, ring up an item that has been set up to require the scale.
entries.quote: Plug the scale into power and turn on the device.

entries.title: Set up the Zebra ZD411 label printer and load labels
steps: Run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the Ethernet port on the back of the label printer.
Connect the supplied power cord.
To load labels, slide the release latches to the front to unlock the cover.
Spread the roll holders open and place the roll in the printer.
Check the roll turns freely and does not sit on the bottom of the media compartment.
Pull the end of the roll past the front edge of the printer.
entries.quote: The roll must not sit in the bottom of

entries.title: Set up Pay at the Table on a PAX device
steps: Turn on the PAX device and open Settings.
Enter the password and select OK. The manual gives 9876 or pax9876@@.
Select Wi-Fi, choose the same network the Paradise station is on, enter the Wi-Fi password and select Connect.
Leave Settings, open the Pay at the Table app on the Home screen and select its Settings icon.
On the Paradise station, log in and go to Admin > Company Settings > Diagnostics and find API IP.
Type that IP address into the Pay at the Table app without the :8123 on the end, then select OK.
entries.quote: The Pay at the Table device and the Paradise station must be on the same network to

entries.title: Log in or clock in on Paradise (employee number or swipe card)
steps: On the login screen, type your personal employee number on the keypad to clock in or out and to log in or out.
If your business uses swipe cards, select Swipe and swipe your card on the card terminal connected to the station.
entries.quote: selecting Swipe will activate the card terminal connected to the station

entries.title: Paradise default employees: Admin and Manager (Manager ID 1234)
steps: A new system shows two default employees in Admin > Employee Maintenance: Admin and Manager.
The Admin employee is meant for tech support access during system issues.
The Manager employee starts with the ID number 1234 and is the account to use when setting up and editing the system.
entries.quote: with the ID number 1234 and should be the account logged in when setting up and editing the

entries.title: Add a new employee login in Paradise
steps: Go to the Admin tab and select Employee Maintenance.
Select New Employee at the top right.
Enter the first and last name, a unique password and a role. These are the only required fields.
To assign the role, select the small plus sign next to Roles and choose a role.
Save the changes.
entries.quote: their first and last name, a unique password, and a role

entries.title: An employee cannot clock in or get into Paradise: check the Active box
steps: Go to Admin > Employee Maintenance and select the employee.
Check the Active setting. If it is deselected the employee is disabled and cannot clock in or access the system.
Select Active again to re-enable the employee and save.
entries.quote: Deselecting it disables the employee, preventing them

entries.title: Stations behaving oddly: check every device is on the same Paradise software version
steps: Look at the software version shown on the login page of each station.
All stations should be on the same version.
Different versions on devices that share one database can cause operating issues.
entries.quote: Different versions of the software on devices that are on the same database

entries.title: Start or end an unpaid break
steps: On the login screen, type your employee number first.
Then select Start Break or End Break.
Your open tickets stay under your employee number while you are on break; break hours are not tracked on the payroll report.
entries.quote: user must type in their employee number first, then select Start/End Break

entries.title: Send an order to the kitchen (Send, Quick Pay, Fast Send, Print & Send)
steps: Send: sends unsent items to the kitchen and clears the ticket from view.
Quick Pay: skips the usual prompts and goes straight to the payment screen.
Fast Send: sends unsent items but keeps the ticket open so you can keep adding items.
Print & Send: prints a receipt and sends unsent items at the same time.
Once items are sent they can no longer be deleted; they must be voided if a change is needed.
entries.quote: Once sent, items can no longer be deleted and must be voided if changes are needed.

entries.title: Take a card payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay at the bottom left to reach the Payment Screen.
Tap Credit. The customer is prompted to pay on the connected card terminal.
When the transaction completes, the credit card receipts print automatically.
Choose the receipt option when asked: No Print, Email or Print.
entries.quote: Prompts the customer to pay via the connected credit card terminal

entries.title: Take a cash payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay.
Enter the amount received on the keypad, or tap one of the preset bill amounts.
Tap Cash.
The cash drawer opens and the screen shows the change due and the receipt options.
entries.quote: The cash drawer will open, and the screen

entries.title: Take a gift card payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay, then Gift Card.
The terminal prompts the customer to use their gift card.
If the card balance does not cover the full amount, the system shows what is still owed so you can pick another payment method for the rest.
entries.quote: doesn’t cover the full amount, the system will display the remaining balance so another

entries.title: Why the Paradise payment screen shows two totals (Total and Cash Total)
steps: If the business uses cash discount or dual pricing, two values show on the payment screen.
Total is the full ticket price.
Cash Total is the price if the customer pays in cash.
entries.quote: The Total is the full ticket price and the Cash Total is the price if paid in cash.

entries.title: Receipt choices after a payment: No Print, Email or Print
steps: After the payment completes, choose No Print, Email or Print.
No Print closes the ticket without a receipt. You can still find the ticket in Ticket Recall and print it from there.
Email asks for an email address to send the receipt to.
Print sends the receipt to the printer assigned to the device. If no printer is assigned, you are asked to pick one.
entries.quote: however to find the ticket in Ticket Recall and print or reprint it from there

entries.title: Reprint a receipt on Paradise
steps: Go to the Manager page and select Ticket Recall.
Use the filters on the left (customer or tab name, ticket ID, employee, date range, price range, SKU or item name) to find the ticket. Ticket Recall covers the past month.
Select the ticket to open the Ticket Admin screen.
Select Print Ticket to print another copy of the receipt.
entries.quote: Print Ticket: Prints another copy of the receipt.

entries.title: Hold an item so it does not go to the kitchen yet
steps: Swipe left to right on the item in the ticket and select Hold.
The item stays on the ticket but is not sent to the kitchen.
To release it, reopen the ticket, swipe on the item again and select Remove Hold, then send the ticket.
entries.quote: To hold an item: Swipe left to right on the item and select Hold.

entries.title: Transfer a ticket or an item to another employee or ticket
steps: Swipe left to right on an item and select Transfer. The employee needs transfer permission.
Choose To Employee to move the whole ticket to another clocked-in employee.
Choose To Ticket to move the whole ticket onto another existing ticket.
Choose Item to move a single item to another ticket.
The ticket or item must already be sent before it can be merged or moved.
entries.quote: must already be sent before it can be merged or transferred

entries.title: Void or comp a single item
steps: Open the ticket.
The item must already be sent. Unsent items can only be deleted.
Swipe the item from right to left.
Tap Comp or Void.
Select a reason from the preset list, or select Other and type one.
entries.quote: The item must be sent—unsent items can only be deleted.

entries.title: Void or comp: which one to use
steps: Use a void when an item or ticket was entered by mistake, usually before the customer received the product.
Use a comp when the customer already received the item or ticket but the business is covering it, for example for food quality or service concerns.
Voids and comps are tracked separately in reports.
entries.quote: Voids are used when an item or ticket was entered by mistake

entries.title: Void a whole ticket
steps: Open the ticket and tap Void Ticket in the bottom-left corner, or go to the Payment Screen and tap Void Ticket at the bottom.
Follow the on-screen prompts.
Select a void reason.
entries.quote: Tap Void Ticket in the bottom-left corner.

entries.title: Comp a whole ticket
steps: Open the ticket.
Go to the Payment Screen.
Select Comp Ticket from the payment options.
Follow the prompts and select a comp reason.
entries.quote: Select Comp Ticket from the payment options.

entries.title: Open a cash drawer at the start of the day
steps: The first employee with drawer access who clocks in is prompted to open the drawer; select Yes. Otherwise go to the Employee screen and select Open Cash Drawer.
Count the starting cash and enter it by denomination, for example enter 5 under $20 for five $20 bills.
Select Confirm. The drawer is now open with its starting funds.
If the physical drawer shut while you were counting, select Open Drawer at the bottom of the prompt.
entries.quote: Open Drawer button at the bottom of the prompt to open it manually

entries.title: Close the cash drawer at the end of the shift or day
steps: First make sure all tickets are closed, shift reports are completed and tips are tipped out.
Go to Employee > Close Cash Drawer and select Close.
Count all the cash in the drawer, including the starting cash, and enter it by denomination. This is a blind count.
Select Confirm, check the total, and select Confirm again.
If the count is right or over, the drawer closes, a drawer report prints and a summary shows on screen.
If the drawer is short, enter a reason. A manager can recount if needed.
entries.quote: count, so be sure to count all cash in the drawer, including the original starting cash

entries.title: Error when closing the cash drawer: tickets still open or shift reports not done
steps: The system shows an error if any tickets are still open or any shift reports are incomplete.
Close or transfer every open ticket.
Have each employee complete their shift report.
Then go back to Employee > Close Cash Drawer.
entries.quote: Note: If any tickets remain open or shift reports are incomplete, the system

entries.title: Swap cash drawers mid-day without closing tickets
steps: Select Close Cash Drawer and choose Swap instead of Close.
Count the whole outgoing drawer and select Confirm. A drawer report prints.
Select Confirm again to move on to the next drawer.
Count the starting cash for the new drawer by denomination and select Confirm.
Every employee who will use the new drawer must select Join Drawer, or their sales will not be recorded under the new drawer.
entries.quote: Important: Any employees who will use the new drawer must select Join Drawer to assign

entries.title: Join or leave a cash drawer
steps: On the Employee page select Join/Leave Drawer.
When you are joined to a drawer your sales count in that drawer's totals.
If you are not joined, your sales are recorded under your own employee number instead of the drawer.
entries.quote: If an employee is not joined to a drawer, their sales are recorded under their individual

entries.title: Record a pay in or pay out (cash added to or taken from the drawer)
steps: A cash drawer must be open on the station.
Select Pay In/Pay Out.
Enter the amount.
Type a reason, and assign a vendor if your system uses vendors.
Select Pay In or Pay Out. The drawer opens so you can put in or take out the cash.
entries.quote: a pay in or pay out, an active cash drawer must be open on the station

entries.title: Check a gift card balance
steps: On the Employee page select Gift Card Balance.
Type the gift card number, or swipe the card on the connected card terminal.
The system shows the balance on the card.
entries.quote: Swipe the gift card using the connected credit card terminal.

entries.title: Look up an item's price (Price Check)
steps: Select Price Check.
Type the item's SKU, or scan the item if a barcode scanner is connected.
entries.quote: Selecting Price Check allows the user to quickly look up the price of an item.

entries.title: Enter or adjust credit card tips
steps: Go to Employee > Tip Adjustment. The screen lists the credit card transactions closed under the logged-in employee.
Select the transaction: tap the blank (0.00) field under the Tip column and a number pad appears.
Type the tip amount.
Repeat for each transaction that needs a tip.
Select Save All Tips. The system then talks to the card terminal to apply the tips.
entries.quote: After all tips have been entered, select Save All Tips on the left side of the screen.

entries.title: Run an employee shift report
steps: Only run it after all your tickets are closed and all tips are adjusted. Only one shift report can be run per shift per employee.
Go to Employee > Shift Report.
Captured Tips at the top shows your credit card tips. Enter any additional declared tips, such as cash tips, in the blank field.
Select Confirm. The shift report prints and a summary shows on screen.
entries.quote: shift report can be run per shift per employee, and it should only be done after all tickets are

entries.title: Reprint an employee shift report or fix a missed clock-in or clock-out
steps: Go to the Manager page and select Shift Maintenance.
Choose By Employee and select the employee to see their shifts.
To reprint a shift report, select the shift and tap Print Report.
If an employee forgot to clock in, select New Shift to create the shift by hand.
To change clock-in or clock-out times, select a closed shift. An open shift must be closed first before it can be edited.
entries.quote: To reprint a shift report, select the employee’s shift and tap Print Report

entries.title: Tip out an employee at the end of their shift
steps: The employee adjusts their credit card tips, closes or transfers all tickets, and runs their shift report. It reads either Employee Owes Restaurant or Restaurant Owes Employee.
Someone assigned to the drawer goes to Employee > Employee Tip Out.
Select the employee marked Has Report.
Enter the amount shown as owed in the blank field.
Tap Tip Out Employee and confirm. The drawer opens and a tip-out slip prints.
If you are tipping yourself out, answer No when asked to clock out so you keep access to the system.
entries.quote: If you’re tipping yourself out, be sure to select No when asked to clock out

entries.title: Kitchen ticket did not print: resend it to the kitchen printer
steps: Open the ticket so it shows in the ticket field.
Go to Employee > Resend Ticket.
The ticket prints again on the assigned kitchen printer.
entries.quote: The system will reprint the ticket to the assigned kitchen printer.

entries.title: How to read a Paradise ticket number
steps: The first 6 digits are the date the ticket was created, as YYMMDD.
The next 3 letters are the device ID of the register that created it.
The next 4 digits are the ticket number.
The last 2 digits identify a split ticket, if there is one.
entries.quote: First 6 digits: Date of ticket creation (YYMMDD)

entries.title: Refund a ticket or individual items
steps: Go to Manager > Ticket Recall and find the ticket.
Select the ticket to open the Ticket Admin screen and select Refund Ticket.
To refund everything choose Refund Ticket; to refund only some items, select them and choose Refund Items.
Choose Give Gift Card to put the refund on a gift card, or Refund All Payments to refund the original payments.
For a card refund the same card must be swiped.
entries.quote: Refund All Payments – Refunds original payment(s); card refunds require

entries.title: Refund without the original receipt (Open Refund)
steps: Create a new ticket with the items being returned, or items matching the refund value. A generic Open Item with Prompt for Price enabled can be used if the original item is not in the system.
Check the return total on the ticket.
Select Open Refund on the Manager page.
Choose Refund Ticket to refund everything, or select items and choose Refund Items.
Choose the refund method. For a card refund the customer must have their card to swipe or insert.
entries.quote: An Open Refund allows a user to issue a refund without requiring the original receipt.

entries.title: A ticket will not close: Force Close is a last resort
steps: Force Close in Ticket Recall closes a ticket without processing a payment.
Paradise describes it as a last resort, often used with tech support guidance.
Used wrongly it can cause reporting discrepancies, so call Paradise tech support before using it.
entries.quote: Force Close: Closes a ticket without processing payment

entries.title: Reopen a closed ticket
steps: Go to Manager > Ticket Recall, find the ticket and select it.
Select Reopen Ticket.
Make the adjustment, such as a void.
Be careful: reopening tickets can affect reports if misused.
entries.quote: Reopen Ticket: Reopens a closed ticket.

entries.title: Look up a current or past cash drawer and reprint its report
steps: Go to Manager > Drawer Recall and filter by date. The To date must be later than the From date or nothing shows.
Select a drawer to see starting cash, cash payments, change given, pay ins and outs, tip ins and outs and the drawer total.
Select Print to reprint the Drawer Report.
If starting cash was entered wrongly, tap the edit icon to recount it, then select Save.
entries.quote: Print: Use this button to reprint the Drawer Report.

entries.title: Drawer Recall shows no results
steps: Check the date filter.
The To date must be later than the From date. If it is not, no results appear.
entries.quote: Be sure the “To” date is later than the “From” date. If not, no results will appear.

entries.title: A cash drawer cannot be closed the normal way: Force Close Drawer
steps: Force Close Drawer in Drawer Recall is only for a drawer that cannot be closed through standard means.
It can disrupt reporting.
Only do it with management or with help from Paradise tech support.
entries.quote: Force Close Drawer: Used only when the drawer cannot be closed through standard means.

entries.title: Batch out credit card transactions by hand (Batch Adjustment)
steps: Go to the Manager page and open Batch Adjustment. It lists all processed credit card transactions that have not yet been batched.
Check every tip has been entered and is correct. You can adjust tips here and change which employee a tip belongs to.
Select the Batch button at the bottom left.
All listed credit transactions are batched out and finalised for deposit.
entries.quote: will manually batch out all listed credit transactions, finalizing them for deposit

entries.title: Tips are missing or wrong and the batch has already gone
steps: Once a batch is processed, tips cannot be adjusted through the POS.
Contact your credit card processor directly.
Have each signed credit slip ready: you will need them to claim or correct the tips.
entries.quote: has already been processed, contact your credit card processor directly

entries.title: A tip was assigned to the wrong employee
steps: Go to Manager > Batch Adjustment before the batch goes out.
Find the transaction.
Select the employee assigned to the tip and change it to the right one.
entries.quote: screen, you have the option to select and change the employee assigned to the tip

entries.title: Add a gratuity to a ticket
steps: Select Add Gratuity on the Manager screen or Add Grat on the Payment Screen. The user needs the right permission.
Apply the gratuity as a percentage or a fixed dollar amount.
The gratuity shows above the total, prints on the customer receipt and is tracked separately from tips.
entries.quote: gratuity to a ticket, either as a percentage or a fixed dollar amount

entries.title: Reset a gift card balance to zero so the card can be reused
steps: Select Manager > Reset Balance.
Swipe the gift card at the terminal when prompted. If you cancel the terminal prompt you can type the card number.
Tick the checkbox next to the card number to see the current balance.
Select Reset Balance and accept the final warning.
This is permanent, cannot be undone, and does not refund earlier payments made with the card.
entries.quote: Note: Resetting a gift card balance is irreversible

entries.title: Split a ticket (by payments, by seat, evenly or by hand)
steps: Open the ticket, then select Employee > Split/Combine Tickets.
Split Payments: enter how many payments to divide the total into and process each one.
Split by Seat: divides the ticket into one ticket per seat; select Done.
Split Evenly: enter the number of splits and select Done.
Manual: tap Split to create a blank ticket, tap an item so it turns green, then tap the destination ticket.
To split one item, swipe left on it, tap Split and enter the number of parts.
entries.quote: split a ticket by item, by seat, split it evenly, or combine tickets together

entries.title: Combine tickets
steps: Open one of the tickets.
Go to Employee > Split/Combine Tickets and select Combine at the bottom right.
Select the other open tickets (same employee) to merge in, or select Scan Tickets if tickets print with barcodes and a scanner is connected.
Tap Combine, then Done.
entries.quote: A new screen will display a list of open tickets assigned to the same employee.

entries.title: Run reports on Paradise
steps: In the app go to Manager > Reports and pick a category. The app holds the past 30 days.
For older data use the online Paradise Dashboard at www.myposdashboard.com.
To get access to the dashboard, contact Paradise POS Tech Support.
Hourly Overview is available straight from the Manager tab.
entries.quote: reporting data beyond this range, the online dashboard must be used

entries.title: Which Paradise reports still work when the network is down
steps: All reports are available in the app while it is connected to the internet.
When the network fails, two reports still work on the device: the Drawer Report when closing a cash drawer, and the employee Shift Report.
entries.quote: However, when the network fails, Paradise has necessary reporting that will still be accessible

entries.title: Taking payments on Paradise when the internet is down (Local Mode)
steps: The setting Allow Payment Offline (Admin > Company Settings, Ticket section) enables several payment methods while the system is offline.
Payment methods that need the credit card terminal are not included.
Allow Splits Offline lets you split tickets offline, but the split shows only on the iPad where it was done, which can cause discrepancies with several iPads.
entries.quote: except for those requiring the credit card terminal

entries.title: Old print jobs are stuck in Open Print Jobs: clear the queue
steps: Go to the Admin page. Open Print Jobs is in the bottom centre. Jobs wait there until a printer becomes available, for example after it was off or out of paper.
Press and hold the top print job and drag your finger down toward the bottom of the page.
A red Clear Queue button appears. Lift your finger and select it.
If many jobs are backed up, repeat this several times.
entries.quote: A red Clear Queue button will appear.

entries.title: Card terminal shows disconnected on the Paradise Admin page: Check Connection
steps: Go to the Admin page and look at Terminal Status.
Select Check Connection. This often reconnects a terminal that was turned off and on or went offline.
When the terminal is connected properly its status shows Available.
A Bluetooth card reader has no IP address listed and may show Label instead of Connected.
entries.quote: If a hardwired terminal appears disconnected, try selecting the Check Connection button on the

entries.title: Print Queue Unavailable
steps: This message in the Printer Status section of the Admin screen most likely means a problem with the internet connection.
Work through the networking troubleshooting steps: check the iPad's Wi-Fi, then restart the modem, router and Pi.
entries.quote: the screen shows Print Queue Unavailable, it likely indicates an issue with the internet connection

entries.title: Printer not printing: check Printer Status on the Admin page first
steps: Go to the Admin page and look at Printer Status at the bottom right.
It lists each Ethernet printer, whether it is online, and its IP address.
It may show the cause, such as out of paper or the tray or cover being open.
entries.quote: it may display that the printer has an error, such as out of paper, or that the tray is open

entries.title: Do not change the default printer settings unless Paradise support says so
steps: Printers shipped from Paradise are usually already created in Admin > Printer Maintenance.
Leave their default settings alone unless tech support tells you to change them. The printers need those settings to work.
entries.quote: The default settings for these printers should remain unchanged unless directed otherwise by

entries.title: An item does not print in the kitchen: assign it to the kitchen printer
steps: Go to Admin > Printer Maintenance and select the kitchen printer.
The list on the right shows the items assigned to that printer.
Tap the small plus sign at the top left of the list to see all items. Use the small i to filter by department or category.
Select the items (or Select All) and tap Add Items to Selected Printer.
Save.
entries.quote: Click Add Items to Selected Printer to assign the selected items to the printer.

entries.title: Receipts go to the wrong printer or ask which printer to use: set the station's Receipt Printer
steps: Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device marked (This Device).
Set Receipt Printer to the printer this station should use for receipts.
Settings shown in grey are locked and cannot be changed.
entries.quote: Receipt Printer: Determines the default printer for this device

entries.title: Customer-facing display not showing: check CFD IP and the network
steps: The iPad stations and the customer-facing display must be on the same network.
Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device.
Check the CFD IP setting. Scanning the QR code on the customer display fills in the IP address automatically.
entries.quote: Both the iPad stations and CFD must be on the same

entries.title: Station keeps returning to the login screen: Device Timeout
steps: Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device.
Device Timeout is the number of seconds before the system returns to the login screen.
Set it to zero to turn the timeout off.
entries.quote: Setting this value to zero will disable the timeout feature.

entries.title: Paradise app frozen on an iPad: close and reopen the app
steps: iPad without a Home button: swipe up from the bottom of the screen and pause in the middle to open the App Switcher.
iPad with a Home button: double-press the Home button to open the App Switcher.
Swipe left or right to find the Paradise app.
Swipe up on the app's preview to close it.
Go back to the Home screen and tap the app icon to reopen it.
entries.quote: Swipe up on the app’s preview to force close it.

entries.title: Paradise app frozen on an Android device: close, reopen or force stop the app
steps: Open the Recent Apps screen (tap the square icon, or swipe up from the bottom and pause).
Find the app and swipe it off the screen to close it.
Go back to the Home screen or app drawer and tap the app icon to reopen it.
If problems continue: open Settings, tap Apps or Apps & notifications, select the app, tap Force Stop and confirm, then reopen the app.
Exact steps vary a little by tablet brand and Android version.
entries.quote: Tap Force Stop, then confirm.

entries.title: Restart an iPad running Paradise
steps: iPad without a Home button: press and hold the Top button and either Volume button until the power off slider appears.
iPad with a Home button: press and hold the Top (or Side) button until the power off slider appears.
Drag the slider to turn the iPad off.
When the screen is completely off, press and hold the Top button again until the Apple logo appears.
entries.quote: Press and hold the Top button and either Volume button until the power off slider appears.

entries.title: Restart an Android device running Paradise
steps: Press and hold the Power button, usually on the side or top.
When the power menu appears, tap Restart or Reboot. If there is no restart option, tap Power Off.
If you chose Power Off, wait until the screen is fully off, then press and hold the Power button until the device starts again.
entries.quote: When the power menu appears on the screen, tap Restart or Reboot.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open and you hear a click
steps: First make sure the drawer is not physically locked.
A clicking sound when you try to open it from the Paradise app means the drawer is likely locked or jammed.
entries.quote: drawer is likely locked or jammed

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open and there is no sound at all
steps: Check the receipt printer is powered on and working. The app opens the drawer through the receipt printer, so if the printer is not working the drawer will not open.
If the printer prints receipts but the drawer still will not open, check the cable between the printer and the drawer.
The cable has two labeled ends. The Cash Drawer end goes into the bottom of the drawer and the Printer end goes into the back of the receipt printer.
entries.quote: Paradise app communicates with the cash drawer through the receipt printer

entries.title: Drawer opens with Open Drawer in the app but not on a cash payment
steps: This usually means no drawer was opened when the station was first used that day.
Go to the Employee screen.
If the button says Open Cash Drawer, no drawer is active. Open one.
Cash taken before a drawer was opened is recorded against the employee instead, and the system shows that employee as owing the restaurant money.
entries.quote: it’s likely that no drawer was opened when the station was first used for the day

entries.title: Bluetooth receipt printer is not printing: first checks
steps: Turn the printer off and back on.
Make sure all cables are connected and secure.
Check paper is loaded correctly in the tray.
Press the Feed button on the front of the printer. If paper feeds through, the paper is installed correctly.
If it still does not print, reconnect the printer to the iPad over Bluetooth.
entries.quote: If paper feeds through, the paper is installed correctly.

entries.title: Reconnect or re-pair a Bluetooth receipt printer to the iPad
steps: Make sure the printer is plugged in and switched on with a steady light on the front panel.
On the iPad Home screen (not inside the Paradise app) tap Settings > Bluetooth and make sure Bluetooth is on.
If the printer shows under My Devices as Not Connected, tap its name. If it changes to Connected you are done.
If it is listed but will not connect, tap the i icon next to its name and select Forget This Device.
With the printer on, press and hold the red Pair button on the back until the indicator light starts flashing, then release.
Wait about 30 seconds. The printer should reappear under My Devices. Tap its name to pair.
The indicator light on the back of the printer turns blue when pairing has worked.
entries.quote: Pair the Printer Again: With the printer still powered on, press and hold the red Pair button

entries.title: Ethernet receipt or kitchen printer is not printing
steps: Check every iPad is on the correct Wi-Fi network, usually named POS - your company name. Open Safari and load a web page to confirm internet access.
If the page does not load, restart your router and Pi.
Open the paper tray, clear any jam, reload the paper, close the tray and hold the Feed button to check paper feeds.
Check all cables on the back of the printer, then turn the printer off and on. The front light should be steady with no flashing error light.
If an error light is on, trace the Ethernet cable from the printer to the router and make sure it is plugged in firmly.
In the Paradise app look for the PQ (Print Queue) indicator at the top of the screen. If it is red, the Pi may need to be restarted.
If all of that is fine, the printer may have a new IP address: print its IP slip and compare it with the app.
entries.quote: for the PQ (Print Queue) indicator. If it’s red, the Pi may need to be restarted

entries.title: Ethernet printer may have a new IP address: print its IP and compare with the app
steps: Turn the printer off.
Hold down the Feed button and turn the printer back on while still holding it.
Keep holding for about 10 seconds. The printer prints a slip with its IP address.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance, select the printer and compare the IP address.
This may not work for every printer brand. Ask Paradise tech support if you need help.
entries.quote: Continue holding for about 10 seconds. The printer will print a slip with its IP

entries.title: USB receipt printer is not printing
steps: Make sure the iPad is connected to the printer with a genuine Apple charging cable. Off-brand cables may not carry both charging and data.
Make sure the printer is on. A solid blue light on the front means it has power.
Open the paper tray, clear any jam, reload the paper, close the tray and press Feed to check it feeds.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Device Maintenance, select This Device and check the correct printer is chosen as the Receipt Printer.
Then go to Admin > Printer Maintenance, select the printer and check its settings.
entries.quote: Off-brand cables may not support both charging and data transfer

entries.title: DHCP Error (card terminal)
steps: A DHCP error means the terminal is offline.
Check the Ethernet cable is firmly connected to both the terminal and the TP-Link router. Try a different port or another cable.
Turn the terminal off, wait 5 seconds and turn it back on. See whether the DHCP error clears.
Make sure the TP-Link router has internet access. Restart your modem and router if the connection problem continues.
entries.quote: A DHCP error indicates the terminal is offline.

entries.title: Card terminal shows Unavailable in the Paradise app (no DHCP error)
steps: The terminal may have the wrong IP address or be on the wrong network.
On the iPad leave the Paradise app, go to Settings > Wi-Fi and connect to your POS network (usually named POS - your company name).
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Terminal Status > Check Connection.
On the terminal press the Menu or Function key. If asked for a password the manual says to try 1234, today's date (for example 05012025 for May 1, 2025) or tomorrow's date.
Go to Communications > LAN Parameters > IP Address.
Compare that IP with the one in the Paradise app under Admin > Terminal Status. If they differ, update the IP address in the Paradise app.
If it still does not work, contact Paradise Tech Support for guided help.
entries.quote: The terminal may have the wrong IP address or may be on the wrong network.
entries.note: Steps vary by terminal model, per the manual.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 1: check the iPad's connection
steps: On the iPad go to Settings > Wi-Fi and make sure it is on the correct network.
Open a web browser and try to load a page.
If the page fails to load, the device is not connected to the internet. Go on to restart the networking equipment.
entries.quote: Open a web browser and try to load a webpage.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 2: restart the modem, router and Pi
steps: Unplug the modem's power for 30 seconds. Plug it back in and wait for the lights to settle, which may take 2 to 3 minutes.
Unplug the TP-Link router for 30 seconds. Plug it back in and wait for it to fully reboot.
If you have a Pi (a small box with a red/green light), disconnect and reconnect its power cord and wait for the lights to turn solid.
entries.quote: Restart the Pi (if applicable): Locate the Pi (small box with a red/green light).

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 3: check each device's network indicator
steps: iPads and Android devices: check the Wi-Fi icon is showing in the top-right corner. Reconnect to the POS network if needed.
Printers: look for a steady green light. Flashing or red means a printer problem.
Card terminals: should show Connected or Ready. If one shows DHCP error, follow the DHCP error steps.
entries.quote: Credit Card Terminals: Should display Connected or Ready.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 4: check Ethernet cables and ports
steps: Check all Ethernet cables are firmly plugged into the correct ports on the modem and router.
Double-check each device is connected to the correct network.
Try plugging the Ethernet cable into another free LAN port on the router.
entries.quote: Try a Different Port: Plug the Ethernet cable into another available LAN port on the router.

entries.title: A device is online but not talking to Paradise: check for IP address conflicts
steps: In the Paradise app go to Admin > Terminal Status.
Compare the IP addresses listed there with the ones printed or displayed by the devices. Duplicate or mismatched IPs can stop communication.
Restart each station, printer and terminal.
entries.quote: Duplicate or mismatched IPs

entries.title: Reset Paradise app connections to terminals and printers
steps: Open the Paradise app.
Go to Admin > Terminal Status.
Tap Check Connection, or Reset Connection if it is offered.
Check all terminals show Available and all printers show Online.
entries.quote: Verify that all terminals show as Available and all printer statuses show as Online.

entries.title: HotSauce Technologies phone number and address
steps: HotSauce Technologies lists its telephone number as 678.325.5300.
Its address is 7001 Peachtree Industrial Blvd Suite 4200, Norcross, GA 30092.
The public site gives no support hours on its home page; its FAQ page says the support department is 24/7.
entries.quote: 7001 Peachtree Industrial Blvd Suite 4200 Norcross, GA 30092

entries.title: HotSauce support is 24/7 and has Spanish, Tagalog and Mandarin speakers
steps: HotSauce describes its support department as 24/7.
Support has Spanish, Tagalog and Mandarin speakers.
The implementation department has Spanish and Tagalog speakers.
entries.quote: For our 24/7 Support Department, we have Spanish, Tagalog, and Mandarin speakers available.

entries.title: HotSauce is sold and serviced through certified resellers
steps: HotSauce POS systems are sold only through its certified reseller channel.
If you have a certified reseller, keep working with them for sales and service.
entries.quote: Hotsauce POS Systems are sold only through our certified reseller channel.

entries.title: Which paper HotSauce printers take
steps: Kitchen printers (impact printers) take 3 inch x 150 foot 1-ply white bond paper, or 3 inch x 90 foot 2-ply carbonless paper.
Kitchen printers also need an ink cartridge. One is supplied with the printer.
Receipt printers (thermal printers) take 3-1/8 inch x 230 foot thermal paper.
The two printers do not use the same paper.
entries.quote: Receipt Printers (Thermal Printer) require 3-⅛” x 230’ Thermal Paper.

entries.title: Where to buy HotSauce printer paper and kitchen ribbons
steps: Order from the HotSauce online store at store.hotsaucepos.com.
Or buy from other distributors, including your food supplier.
HotSauce does not supply free POS paper.
entries.quote: Hotsauce does not supply free pos paper

entries.title: Internet is down on HotSauce: offline payments must be switched on by hand
steps: Offline payments are not automatic. If the internet goes down, the settings have to be changed manually.
Understand the risk before you do: while processing offline you will not know whether a card was declined until the system is connected to the internet again.
The public FAQ does not say where the setting is, so contact HotSauce support to change it.
entries.quote: If the internet goes down, the settings will have to be changed manually.

entries.title: HotSauce training mode: card payments do not go through and nothing is saved
steps: A HotSauce system is not delivered in training mode. It is only turned on at the owner's request.
In training mode card transactions do not go through and transactions are not saved on the system.
entries.quote: Card transactions will not go through nor will the transactions save on the system.

entries.title: Where HotSauce reports are and how to print them
steps: The HotSauce back office is only on the SERVER terminal.
Have the reports emailed to you, or print them on the receipt printer attached to that terminal.
Reports away from the restaurant need the add-on Mission Control: Reporting.
entries.quote: Hotsauce Back office is set on only the SERVER terminal.

entries.title: HotSauce is not cloud based: the data is held on the POS terminal
steps: The HotSauce system is not cloud based.
All of the information is held only on the POS terminal.
entries.quote: All of the information is only held on the POS terminal.

entries.title: Why HotSauce needs its own router
steps: HotSauce says PCI compliance requires a specific router to be used with its system.
Keep the HotSauce router in place; it is also how HotSauce keeps the system private and secure.
entries.quote: PCI Compliance requires a specific router be used with our system.

entries.title: HotSauce stations are touch screens; the back office server needs a mouse and keyboard
steps: All server POS stations are touch screens.
The Back Office Server computer needs a mouse and keyboard.
entries.quote: The Back Office Server computer will require a mouse and keyboard.

entries.title: Start a bar tab with the PAX S300 chip reader on HotSauce
steps: Tap Start a Tab. You can enter a name, swipe a card, or start the tab with the chip reader.
If you start the tab with the chip reader, you still need to enter the name or swipe the card on the terminal, because the chip reader does not pull a name.
entries.quote: as the chip reader does not pull a name

entries.title: HotSauce manager cards and the 4 digit PIN
steps: Staff clock in and get into the front of house with a 4 digit PIN.
A manager card works the same way as the PIN: you swipe the card instead of typing.
entries.quote: They work the same way as the 4 digit pin, except you just have to swipe the card!

entries.title: HotSauce PAX A920 handheld has weak or no signal
steps: The A920 gets its signal from a wireless access point.
More than one wireless access point may be needed to cover the floor. Ask HotSauce or your reseller about adding one.
entries.quote: A920 gets signal from Wireless Access Point. More than 1 Wireless Access Point may be needed

entries.title: HotSauce A920: the chip reader is always active
steps: The A920 is a wireless card terminal used to order and pay at the table.
It cannot be used without the chip reader; the chip reader is always active.
entries.quote: The chip reader will always be active.

entries.title: UberEats, GrubHub and other delivery orders on HotSauce are entered by hand
steps: HotSauce is not integrated with any third party delivery service.
HotSauce can set up payment buttons labeled with each delivery service you use.
The orders themselves have to be entered into the POS by hand.
entries.quote: HotSauce is not currently integrated with any third party delivery service.

entries.title: HotSauce online orders print in the kitchen automatically
steps: An online order prints to the kitchen automatically.
The front of house also shows notifications in several places so servers and the host know an online order came in.
The wait time sent to customers can be controlled on the main POS terminal.
entries.quote: It automatically prints to the kitchen, which is why our online ordering requires credit card payment

entries.title: An imported (older) gift card will not swipe on HotSauce
steps: Imported cards may not swipe, depending on which track of the magnetic stripe holds the data.
Type the full card number instead.
entries.quote: In this case, you would type the full number of the previous cards in order to use them.

entries.title: HotSauce does not install on your own computer
steps: HotSauce does not install on any third party hardware.
For a back office computer for reports and menu edits, the Elite Server has to be added to the contract.
entries.quote: Hotsauce doesn't install on any 3rd party hardware.

entries.title: HotSauce staff training videos
steps: HotSauce's FAQ page links training videos: Full Service in English, Full Service in Spanish, Quick Counter Service / Bar in English, and Handheld A920.
Open the FAQs page on hotsaucepos.com to reach them.
entries.quote: Quick Counter Service / Bar - English

entries.title: Genius for Restaurants support: 24/7/365 phone and email
steps: Genius for Restaurants support is open 24/7/365.
Call 800-3Genius.
Or email GeniusRestaurantSupport@globalpay.com.
entries.quote: Hours: 24/7/365 800-3Genius GeniusRestaurantSupport@globalpay.com

entries.title: Genius Enterprise support channels (SMS, chat, phone, email)
steps: SMS 1-844-957-4434 for critical issues where pictures or detailed steps help, such as network or hardware issues.
Phone 1-800-547-4266 for emergencies or complex issues, such as network cables, credit card processing or offline equipment.
Email sos@globalpay.com for non-critical issues or questions.
WebChat and Web-to-Case are also offered through the support-request link on the Genius Contact Support page.
entries.quote: Example: Issues with network cables, credit card processing, or offline equipment. 1-800-547-4266
entries.note: This page is headed Contact Genius Enterprise Support; restaurant merchants are given 800-3Genius in the XC23 guide.

entries.title: Global Payments general support numbers by portfolio (US and Canada)
steps: USA Global Payments: +1-800-688-5378.
USA Heartland: +1-888-963-3600.
Canada Global Payments: +1-800-263-2970.
No hours are given on the page.
entries.quote: USA Global Payments +1-800-688-5378

entries.title: Older Heartland Restaurant support line (2020 FAQ)
steps: The 2020 FAQ lists a 24/7 support phone, 1-833-844-HPOS (4767).
It also lists the email HRPOSSupport@heartland.us.
Use the current Genius numbers first; this entry is here in case a merchant quotes the old line.
entries.quote: 24/7 Support Phone: 1-833-844-HPOS(4767)
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Genius GC26 countertop: what is in the box
steps: The GC26 arrives assembled.

Check for: the 15.6-inch merchant-facing display, counter-top stand, removable plastic top cover, magnetic metal front cable cover, port hub, USB-C cable for the display, power supply and power cable.
An optional 10.1-inch customer-facing display may be included, with or without a payment reader, either on a bracket on the stand or on its own low-profile stand.
entries.quote: 15.6-inch Merchant Facing Display (MFD)

entries.title: Set up the Genius GC26 countertop station
steps: Remove and discard the shipping tape and covers from the displays, stand and cables.
Tilt the merchant display back and pull off the magnetic cable cover on the stand to reveal the port hub.
Feed the power cord, Ethernet, cash drawer and USB cables up through the hole in the bottom of the stand and plug them into the port hub.
If a customer display was ordered it is already plugged into the top USB-C port; check that cable is properly seated.
Refit the front cable cover: angle the top in first and let the magnets connect.
Take off the black top cover and check the display cables are seated at the back under the display arm and in the top of the stand, then refit the cover.
Adjust the screens, then plug the power cable into an outlet.
Press the power button on the lower-left back corner of the merchant display. It lights blue when the display is on.
After boot-up the GC26 launches the Genius app. Set up Wi-Fi and the Genius app.
entries.quote: Power on the MFD by locating the power button on the lower-left back corner of the MFD.

entries.title: Genius GC26 display does not power on
steps: Check the power supply connections.
Check the electrical outlet it is plugged into.
Make sure all cables are in their correct ports in the hub and firmly seated.
entries.quote: If the display does not power on, check the power supply connections and the corresponding electrical outlet.

entries.title: Genius GC26 on Ethernet is not connecting
steps: Make sure all cables are connected to their correct ports in the hub and are firmly seated.
Verify network connectivity for the Ethernet connection.
entries.quote: Verify network connectivity for Ethernet connections.

entries.title: Enable a location for Genius on XC23, GC26 (NextGen) or Mobile 2.0 devices
steps: Only registered devices can access Genius Restaurant at a location.
In a web browser, log into the Admin Portal for your account and location.
From the Main Menu select Location Setup, then the Mobile/NextGen Settings tab.
Select Add Location to Mobile NextGen Group.
Force close and restart the Restaurant app on all other devices on the network, including tablets and kiosks. This resets their socket connection.
entries.quote: This action resets the socket connection of the device and helps to avoid disruptions to performance.

entries.title: XC23: reach the ports to attach a printer, customer display or other peripherals
steps: At the back of the XC23, under the display, find the access opening to the drive.
Find the plastic cover that holds the drive chassis. Two screws under the chassis secure it.
Remove the screws with a Phillips screwdriver and set them aside.
Attach the peripherals to the appropriate ports.
Put the plastic cover back and secure it with the screws.
entries.quote: Two screws, located under the drive chassis, secure the cover.

entries.title: A peripheral on the XC23 is dead: check the XC23 base is powered on
steps: Some peripherals are powered over USB from the XC23.
Make sure the XC23 base is powered on, or those peripherals will not work properly.
entries.quote: require that the XC23 base is powered on in order for the peripherals to function properly

entries.title: Connect the receipt printer to an XC23 and load paper
steps: Plug the power cable into the printer.
Plug the USB-B end of the data cable into the printer and the USB-A end into the XC23 drive.
Thread the cables through the access panels and plug the power cable into an outlet.
Open the paper feed lid.
Insert the paper roll so the paper feeds from the bottom of the roll.
Close the lid and flip the power switch on.
entries.quote: Insert paper roll so that paper feeds from the bottom of the roll.

entries.title: Receipt paper size for the Genius XC23 receipt printer
steps: Use paper 80mm wide, 0.053 to 0.085mm thick, with a roll diameter of up to 83mm.
A USB thermal receipt printer cannot currently be used as a shared kitchen printer.
entries.quote: The receipt printer uses printer paper that is 80mm wide

entries.title: Connect the cash drawer on a Genius station
steps: Turn the cash drawer over to reach its ports.
Plug the cable end marked Cash Drawer into the cash drawer.
Plug the other end, marked Printer, into the receipt printer's data port.
entries.quote: Plug the other end marked Printer into the printer data port.

entries.title: Connect the barcode scanner to an XC23
steps: Plug the RJ45 end of the cable into the scanner charging cradle.
Plug the USB end into one of the black USB-A ports on the XC23 drive.
Scan the QR code that comes with it.
Wait for the scanner to chirp twice, the green light to flash, and the scanner to chirp once more.
entries.quote: Plug the USB end of the cable into one of the black colored USB-A ports on the XC23 drive.

entries.title: Fit the ribbon and paper in the Genius kitchen printer
steps: Open the ribbon cassette cover using the tabs on each side.
Unpack the ribbon cassette and turn its knob to take up the slack.
Insert the cassette and push down until it clicks into place, then close the cover.
Open the paper feed lid and insert the roll so paper feeds from the bottom of the roll.
Close the lid, plug the power cable into an outlet and flip the power switch on.
entries.quote: Insert the new ribbon cassette, then push down until it clicks into place.

entries.title: Connect the Genius POS Reader to an XC23
steps: The POS Reader is plug and play and needs no Admin Portal setup.
Attach its cable to the XC23 drive.
Stay on the reader login PIN screen until all firmware updates finish. This can take up to three minutes.
entries.quote: This payment device is considered Plug and Play (PnP) and does not require Admin Portal configuration.

entries.title: Card swiped but the Reader shows a status panel: it is still initializing
steps: The payment device re-initializes when the POS app first runs, after the device restarts, after a Publish update from the Admin Portal, after the app cache is cleared, or after the app is reinstalled.
Stay on the PIN screen for 2 to 3 minutes to let it finish.
If you swiped while it was still initializing, tap Cancel to close the panel and go back to Checkout.
Swipe the card again once the device has finished initializing.
entries.quote: we recommend you remain on the PIN screen for 2-3 minutes

entries.title: Connect power to a Verifone T650C used with Genius
steps: On the bottom of the device, press the release button and slide off the protective plate.
Connect the power supply cable to the power port. Connect an Ethernet cable if you use one.
Replace the plate and plug the power cable into an outlet.
Then connect the device to the network.
entries.quote: From the bottom of the device, press the release button then slide off the protective plate.

entries.title: Connect a Verifone T650C or T650P to Wi-Fi for Genius
steps: Power on the device and tap the Home icon.
At the bottom of the screen tap the ^ icon.
Select Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi.
Select the Wi-Fi network. It should be the same network the POS is on.
Type the Wi-Fi password and tap Connect.
Write down the IP address assigned to the device. It is needed in the Admin Portal.
The T650C can use Wi-Fi or Ethernet. The T650P can only use Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: The T650C may connect to the network via WiFi or Ethernet. The T650P may only connect through WiFi.

entries.title: Connect a Verifone T650C to Ethernet for Genius
steps: Ethernet needs the additional charging base.
Power on the device, tap the Home icon and tap the ^ icon at the bottom of the screen.
Select Settings > Network & Internet > Advanced Options > Ethernet.
Select DHCP or Static.
For Static, enter the IP address, gateway, network prefix length (24 by default), DNS 1 and DNS 2.
Tap Save.
entries.quote: Select Settings > Network & Internet > Advanced Options > Ethernet

entries.title: A Verifone T650 cannot share a terminal with a PAX or CFD device
steps: You cannot run a Verifone T650 with a PAX or customer-facing display device on the same terminal.
entries.quote: NOTE: You cannot run a Verifone T650 device with a PAX or CFD device on the same terminal.

entries.title: Get a Device Login Code for a new or logged-out Genius device
steps: Connect the device to the network.
Log into the Admin Portal and open the right location.
In the Main Menu click Location Setup, then Authorized Tablets.
Click the Login Code tab and click Generate Code.
The same code can log in multiple POS, KDS or kiosk apps. For a new code select Regenerate Code.
entries.quote: New devices at a location require a Device Login Code.

entries.title: Sign a device in to the Genius POS
steps: Connect the device to the network and let it finish updating. It reboots and opens Genius for Restaurants.
On the XC23 Home screen tap the Genius icon if the app is not open.
Enter a valid Device Login Code and tap Confirm.
When asked how the device will be used, tap Permanent.
On the PIN screen enter a valid PIN and tap Go.
entries.quote: After submitting a login code, the POS will prompt you to specify how the device will be used.

entries.title: Genius login (authorization) codes: how long they last and how they work
steps: For merchants a new code is valid for one hour.
While valid, one code can log in several devices and apps (POS, KDS and Kiosk).
Codes belong to the location, not to a device.
Device Licensing Codes are six alphanumeric characters.
Staff still use their normal PINs on the PIN screen once the device is logged in.
entries.quote: For merchants, new authorization codes remain valid for one (1) hour.

entries.title: A Genius device got logged out and nobody on site can get into the Admin Console
steps: A logged-out POS, KDS or Kiosk needs an authorization code to log back in.
If staff cannot reach the Admin Console to get one, ask the dealer or the Genius Support department for a temporary login code for the location.
entries.quote: they can request a temporary login code for that location from either the dealer or the Genius Support department

entries.title: Genius Admin Console sign-in codes (multi-factor authentication)
steps: Everyone who logs into the Admin Console must enter an authentication code; there is no opt-out.
The first code is emailed. After that you can choose text message, email or an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator or Google Authenticator).
You can ask the Admin Console to remember a code for up to 45 days.
Login passwords do not expire.
entries.quote: you can ask the program to “remember” it for up to 45 days

entries.title: Do not tap System Logout by mistake: it needs a Device Login Code to get back in
steps: Logout (lower right of the Room screen) only logs the staff member out and shows the PIN screen.
System Logout (last option in the Manager Settings menu) logs the whole device out of the account and shows the Account Login screen.
After a System Logout someone must enter a valid Device Login Code for the account to get back into the POS.
entries.quote: will need to enter a valid Device Login Code for the account

entries.title: Cannot sign in to a new Genius POS: Staff users have not been created
steps: You cannot sign in to the point of sale until Staff users have been created in the Guided Setup process.
Check your inbox for the Account Activation email and start the Guided Setup.
entries.quote: until you have created Staff users during the Guided Setup process

entries.title: XC23 first power-on: connect to the internet and wait for updates
steps: Feed the power cable through the openings on the bottom of the stand and press the power button on the back of the device.
Wi-Fi (recommended): when first turned on the device asks you to select a wireless network. Select it and enter the password.
If that prompt disappears, turn the device off and back on to get it again.
Ethernet: route the network cable through the bottom access port and the cable channel in the neck of the stand and connect it to the Ethernet port.
Let the device download and install its updates. This can take 15 to 30 minutes depending on network speed.
entries.quote: If the prompt disappears, you will need to turn the device off and back on to access the prompt again.

entries.title: Genius NextGen or Mobile 2.0 device will not join the Wi-Fi: WPA3 is not supported
steps: NextGen devices and Mobile 2.0 handhelds do not support the WPA3 security standard.
Set the Wi-Fi network to WPA2 (or WEP) for these devices.
entries.quote: Note: NextGen devices do not support WPA3 security standard.

entries.title: Connect an XC23 to Wi-Fi from its settings
steps: Go to the XC23 Home screen and tap the Settings icon.
Tap Network & internet, then Wi-Fi.
Select the network, enter its password and tap Connect.
entries.quote: In the Network & internet screen, tap Wi-Fi.

entries.title: Power up a Genius NextGen device
steps: Press and hold the Power button on the underside of the screen.
When it has powered up it shows its Home screen.
entries.quote: Press and hold the Power button (on the underside of the screen).

entries.title: No content is configured for this device.
steps: This blue-screen message appears when the NextGen stand's Network prompt timed out before a Wi-Fi network was selected.
Restart the NextGen device manually.
When the Network screen shows again, select the Wi-Fi network and connect straight away.
entries.quote: No content is configured for this device.

entries.title: NextGen device stuck on the blue 'device setup is completed' screen
steps: After its update utilities run, the device shows a blue screen with a spinning icon and then restarts. This normally takes 5 to 15 minutes.
If it has not restarted by itself after 15 minutes, restart the device manually.
entries.quote: if the device does not restart on its own after 15 minutes, you should restart the device manually

entries.title: Customer display or NextGen screen does not display properly: set screen density to 160
steps: Tap the Home button in the bottom panel, then tap the Settings icon on the Apps screen.
Tap Display, then Advanced.
Tap Screen density and select 160 MDPI.
Tap REBOOT NOW when prompted. The device restarts with the new density.
Do this before signing into the Genius POS app.
entries.quote: Tap Screen density, then select 160 MDPI.

entries.title: Update the Genius POS app on a NextGen device
steps: Turn on the device and run the POS app.
On the PIN screen tap the Information icon in the lower left corner.
In the Information panel tap Check for Update.
If there is no update the POS briefly shows Resync Complete.
If there is one it downloads and installs straight away, which can take several minutes. The POS then restarts and shows the PIN screen.
entries.quote: In the Information panel, tap Check for Update.

entries.title: Do not remove the blue or black pull tabs on the USB-C cables
steps: Some USB-C cables supplied with the NextGen device have small plastic pull tabs on their ends.
Leave them on. They give you grip to pull the cable out of the inner housing of the device.
entries.quote: Do not remove these blue tabs from their cables.

entries.title: Customer-facing display beeps but shows a black screen
steps: Find the circular button on the back of the customer display.
Press and hold it until the screen flashes on.
entries.quote: If your CFD beeps but does not display anything, find the circular button on the back of the device.

entries.title: Connect the customer-facing display to a NextGen terminal
steps: Turn the customer display over and unspool its USB-C power cable.
Slide the back panel off the NextGen device to reveal the USB-C port labeled CFD.
Plug the cable into the CFD port and refit the back panel, threading the cable through its access hole.
Power on the NextGen device and log into the POS. The customer display then shows a smaller version of the POS screen.
entries.quote: This will reveal a USB-C printer port labeled CFD.

entries.title: Set which printers a Genius station uses (printer template and Default Register Printer)
steps: Log into the POS and tap the Options button on the Rooms screen.
Tap Settings, then Printers.
Tap New Template, name it and select the rooms that use the printer on this device.
Tap Enable on each printer this device will use. Tap Send Test on a printer's tile to send a test print.
Tap Save, then select the template and tap Use.
Select the Default Register Printer, then tap Exit.
entries.quote: To send a test print job to an enabled printer, tap Send Test in the printer’s tile.

entries.title: Guest checks will not print or the cash drawer will not open: no Default Register Printer set
steps: Each station needs a default register printer to print guest checks or use an attached cash drawer.
Open the Manager Settings menu and tap Printers.
Select a printer template with Use, or create one, and choose the Default Register Printer for this device.
entries.quote: The POS requires a default register printer in order to print guest checks or use an attached cash drawer.

entries.title: Printing problem on Genius: open the Printer Queue panel
steps: On the Room screen tap the Printer Queue button.
The panel describes the printer's current status in detail.
entries.quote: Printer Queue: This button displays a panel that describes the printer's current status in detail.

entries.title: Add an Ethernet or Wi-Fi printer in the Genius Admin Portal
steps: USB-attached printers need no configuration. Ethernet and Wi-Fi printers do.
In the Admin Console click Location Setup, then Printers, then +New.
Type a name and the printer's IP address. For kitchen printers also select Shared.
Select the Printer Brand and Printer Series, then Save.
Select the Upload icon to publish the change and answer Yes.
entries.quote: USB-attached printers do not require configuration.

entries.title: Set a backup printer for when a kitchen printer fails
steps: In the POS go to Options > Settings > Printers and open the printer template.
On each enabled printer, use the Backup printer for formats area to choose the display formats that should fall back to this printer.
Save the template.
entries.quote: as their backup when their default printer ever fails or loses its connection

entries.title: Epson TM-U220 kitchen printer: print the network status sheet (find its IP address)
steps: Make sure the printer is turned on.
Turn the printer around and push the pinhole reset button on the back with a pen or pencil tip for four seconds.
A status sheet prints with the printer's IP address on your network.
entries.quote: push the pinhole reset button on the back of the printer for four seconds

entries.title: Epson TM-U220 status sheet shows IP 192.168.192.168: the printer is not on your network yet
steps: 192.168.192.168 is the Epson default address. It means an older static model that is not yet connected to your network.
It has to be switched to DHCP from a device temporarily set to the printer's address range.
On the iOS device go to Settings > Wi-Fi, tap the information icon by the network, tap Configure IP, select Manual and set the IP address to 192.168.192.100.
Open a browser to 192.168.192.168 and log in. The guide gives username epson and password epson; if that fails the password is the device serial number in capitals.
Under Configuration open TCP/IP and change Acquire the IP Address to Auto, then click Send.
Turn the printer off and on, print the status sheet again to confirm, then set the iOS device's Configure IP back to Auto.
entries.quote: then the printer is an older model known as static and not yet connected to your network

entries.title: Connect an Epson TM-U220 kitchen printer by Ethernet for Genius
steps: Turn the printer off with the power button.
Connect the Ethernet cable between the printer and your internet router.
Turn the printer on.
Push the pinhole reset button on the back for 4 seconds with a pen or pencil tip. A status sheet prints with the printer's IP address.
Add the printer in the Admin Portal under Printers with that IP address, then save and publish.
entries.quote: A status sheet should auto-print with the printer’s IP address on your network.

entries.title: Star SP700 kitchen printer: print the status page (find its IP address)
steps: Load paper and turn the printer off.
Hold the Feed button while turning the power on, and keep holding as it powers up.
After several seconds the power lights come on and it beeps once. Release Feed after the first beep.
The Printer Status page prints, then the network information.
The IP address is in the Current IP Parameters Status section at the bottom of the second printout.
entries.quote: After the first beep, release the Feed.

entries.title: Star SP700: reset the printer with the RST button
steps: With paper loaded and the printer on, the green POWER light is on.
Hold the RST button on the back with a small tool for more than five seconds.
The front lights flash while it resets, then the light turns solid green.
entries.quote: If you hold the [RST] button on the back of the printer with a small tool for more than five seconds

entries.title: Star SP700: set a static IP address
steps: On a computer or tablet on the same network, open a browser to the IP address shown on the Printer Status page.
Click Login. The guide gives the default username root and password public.
Select IP Parameters, then Static, and enter the IP address, subnet mask and default gateway.
Click Submit, then Save, select Save configuration printing restart device and click Execute.
The printer restarts and prints the status page.
entries.quote: Select IP Parameters on the left, then select Static.

entries.title: Wi-Fi receipt printer setup failed: you did not wait for the lights to stop blinking
steps: The error means the printer had not finished updating.
Start the Wi-Fi setup step again.
This time wait until all the lights on the printer stop blinking while it receives its configuration.
entries.quote: wait until all lights stop blinking on the printer while it is receiving configuration

entries.title: Epson Wi-Fi receipt printer: print its network interface information
steps: With the printer off, hold the feed button.
While holding it, power the printer on.
A slip prints with the Wi-Fi and Ethernet interface information.
Press the feed button once more to print a self test.
entries.quote: A slip will print with the WiFi & Ethernet interface information.

entries.title: Epson TM-L90 label printer is not feeding labels correctly: format it for the label size
steps: Turn the printer off and open the roll paper cover. Leave it open.
Turn the printer on, then off again with the cover open.
Turn it on while pressing and holding Feed, with the cover still open, until the error and power lights are on.
Press the feed button six times.
Close the cover. The printer should feed labels by itself to learn the label size.
If it does not feed when the cover is closed, the process went wrong: start over.
entries.quote: If the printer will not feed paper automatically when closing the cover, the process was done
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: All printing stopped on a Genius iPad system: the Dedicated Socket Server is down
steps: If the iPad set as the Dedicated Socket Server goes down, all printing goes down, and the other devices stop syncing tickets to the cloud.
Get that iPad running and connected again.
If you have several iPads, another one can be set as the Dedicated Socket Server and it takes over.
entries.quote: If the iPad designated as the Dedicated Socket Server goes down, will all printing go down?
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: A Genius printer has locked up
steps: Restart the printer. The FAQ says restarting is the only way to clear a locked-up printer.
Lockups and lost jobs are a known risk of the Shared Printing without Sockets setting, which Global Payments says not to use in normal operation.
entries.quote: If a printer locks up the only way to troubleshoot it is to restart
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Where a report prints when you tap Print in the Genius POS app
steps: Print in the POS app sends the report to the default register printer set for that device under Manager > Printers.
Print in the Admin Portal opens your browser's own print settings instead.
entries.quote: will route to the configured
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Take payment on a Genius ticket (card, cash, gift card)
steps: Open the ticket and tap Checkout to reach the Payment screen.
For a credit card tap Card. For a gift card tap Gift Card. For a custom tender tap Custom.
For exact cash tap Cash.
If the customer hands over more cash, enter the amount on the keypad or tap a suggested amount. The POS shows the change due.
entries.quote: If the customer pays with a credit card, tap Card. If the customer pays with a gift card, tap Gift Card.

entries.title: Void a whole ticket on Genius
steps: Open the ticket and tap Actions.
Tap Void Order.
Tap a void reason, and add a description if you want.
Tap Void. The ticket is voided and its table shows as available.
entries.quote: To void the whole ticket, tap an appropriate void reason, then tap Void.

entries.title: Refund a paid ticket on Genius
steps: Open the paid ticket, tap Actions, then Refund. Refund appears only after a ticket is paid and refunds the full amount.
Tap OK at the Refund Ticket prompt.
Select a refund reason or type one, then tap Refund.
Choose how to pay the refund: Cash, Card, Gift Card (if enabled) or Custom.
The POS processes the refund and shows a screen confirming approval. Tap Print for a receipt.
A refunded ticket shows its items in red text and its tile is highlighted red.
