entries.quote: The Refund action enables you to refund the full amount of a ticket back to a customer

entries.title: Reprint a ticket or receipt on Genius
steps: Open the ticket and tap Actions, then Reprint.
Tap the button for the printer you want. The ticket is sent to that printer.
Press and hold a printer's button to get a Preview option.
entries.quote: If you tap a printer button, the POS will send the ticket to the selected printer.

entries.title: Apply or remove a discount on a Genius ticket
steps: Open the ticket, tap Actions, then Discounts.
Tap a discount. For an open-amount discount enter the amount on the keypad and tap Apply.
To remove it, tap the discount in the ticket panel and tap Remove Discount.
entries.quote: If you need to remove the discount from the ticket, tap the discount in the ticket panel, then tap Remove Discount.

entries.title: Move a ticket to another server on Genius
steps: Open the ticket, tap Actions, then Change Server.
Select the server (only clocked-in servers are listed) and tap Go.
If you do not see the server, type the name in the Server Name box.
entries.quote: To assign the ticket to a new server, select an appropriate server’s button, then tap Go.

entries.title: Find a ticket on Genius
steps: On the Room screen tap Tickets.
Type a ticket number, customer name or card number in the Search box.
Or filter by Servers, Statuses, Service Areas or Payments. Tap Clear Filters to reset.
entries.quote: To search for a specific ticket, enter a ticket number, customer name, or card number in the Search box.

entries.title: Open the cash drawer without a sale (No Sale)
steps: On the Rooms screen tap the Options button in the top right corner.
Tap No Sale.
This only works if your job type has access to the cash drawer and the No Sale permission.
entries.quote: The POS will only perform this task if you are in a job type with access to the cash drawer

entries.title: Record a pay in or pay out on Genius
steps: Open the Pay In/Out section and select the cash pay type.
Enter the amount. Add a comment if needed.
Tap Pay In or Pay Out.
entries.quote: If you want to perform a “pay out” transaction, tap Pay Out.

entries.title: Card reader not responding: check its status and re-select the payment terminal
steps: On the Rooms screen tap the Card Reader icon. A panel lists the status of the card readers; a working one shows CONNECTED.
If it is not connected, open Options > Settings > Payment Terminals.
Tap the tile of the terminal for this station (available ones show light green). The POS tries to connect to it.
entries.quote: If the POS connected successfully, the list will display its status as CONNECTED.

entries.title: Add a payment terminal (not the POS Reader) to Genius
steps: In the Admin Portal go to Location Setup > Payment Terminals and select +New.
Type a name and the IP address of the payment device, then Save.
Select the Upload icon to publish.
In the POS select Menu > Manager > Payment Terminals and select the terminal.
entries.quote: The following is required for all payment devices other than the POS Reader.

entries.title: Payments are not processing or orders are not syncing: check Training Mode is off
steps: Open Options > Settings > General.
Check the Training Mode switch.
In training mode the POS does not process payments or sync its orders with other devices. Turn it off for live service.
entries.quote: While running in training mode, the POS will not process any payments performed on it

entries.title: Change how quickly the Genius POS logs out when idle
steps: Open Options > Settings > General.
In the Auto Logout section pick a duration: 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, or 1 hour.
entries.quote: the POS will automatically log out if it is idle for the selected duration of time

entries.title: Mark an item out of stock (86) on Genius
steps: Open Options > Settings > Item Stock Management.
Search for the item and set its count to 0, then tap Save.
Out-of-stock items show in red and cannot be ordered in the POS or on the Online Order website.
entries.quote: To designate an item as out of stock, set the item’s stock value to “0”.

entries.title: Fix a clock-in or clock-out on Genius (Time Punch Management)
steps: Open Options > Settings > Time Punch Management.
Set the date range, and filter by Staff or Job Type if needed.
Tap Edit on the time punch, then tap the Clock In or Clock Out tile to set a new date or time.
Tap Save. To delete a punch, swipe left and tap Delete.
entries.quote: Once you have made the necessary edit to the time punch, tap its Save button to save the new settings.

entries.title: Each Genius device needs its own ticket prefix
steps: Set the prefix under Options > Settings > Tablets: one to four characters, then Save.
If you use prefixes, every POS device must have a unique one. Letters are recommended.
entries.quote: If you use ticket prefixes, you must use a unique prefix for each POS device.

entries.title: End of day on Genius: clear the Daily Review screen
steps: Tap the Options button, then Settings, then Daily Review.
The screen has three tabs: Tips, Tickets and Cash. A tab with unresolved transactions shows a red mark.
Tickets: open each ticket that is not closed and close it.
Tips: enter the missing tips, or tap Empty Tips then Mark empty tips as 0, then tap Submit Tips.
Cash: check every server bank and cash drawer has been checked out.
entries.quote: The Daily Review screen enables managers to quickly review what transactions are left to be resolved during end-of-day procedures.

entries.title: Transactions will not batch at end of day: tips have not been captured (Auth/Capture)
steps: If your card processing is set to Auth/Capture, tips must be captured for a transaction to batch out at the end of the day.
Open Daily Review and tap the Tips tab. A red X means tips are still outstanding.
Enter each tip, or mark empty tips as 0, then tap Submit Tips.
With Sale/Adjust processing the indicator does not show because it is not required for end of day.
entries.quote: If your credit card processing is set to Auth/Capture tips must be captured to batch a transaction out at the end of day.

entries.title: Enter tips on closed card transactions (Daily Review > Tips)
steps: Open Daily Review and tap the Tips tab. It lists transactions closed without a tip.
Tap the ticket's Tip box, enter the amount on the keypad and tap Done.
To set every empty tip to $0, tap Empty Tips, then Mark empty tips as 0.
Tap Submit Tips to save.
entries.quote: When you have finished editing tip amount for all necessary tickets, tap Submit Tips.

entries.title: A server did not check out: Force Server Checkout
steps: Open Daily Review and tap the Cash tab. Banks not checked out show a red Report button.
Tap the Report button and then Force Server Checkout at the bottom of the report.
This only works if all of that server's tickets are closed. If any are open the POS shows an error, so close them first.
entries.quote: If all tickets are closed, the POS will allow you to force the checkout. If any tickets are still open, the POS will display an error.

entries.title: Server checkout at the end of a shift
steps: Close all of your tickets, or transfer them to another staff member.
Tap Checkout and confirm.
Hand any amount shown as Server Owes Merchant to the restaurant. If the amount is negative, the restaurant pays that amount to the server.
A manager can review the checkout in Daily Review.
entries.quote: the server should return any amount listed as Server Owes Merchant to the restaurant

entries.title: Tip out to another staff member on Genius
steps: On the Room screen tap the Options button, then Tip Out.
On the Tip tab, under Tip Out From, choose the pool (My Tips is the default).
Under Tip Out To choose Staff, pick the job type and the staff member's name.
Type the dollar amount, add a comment if you want, and tap Tip Out.
Tap OK to confirm.
entries.quote: In the Amount box, type the dollar amount of the tip out.

entries.title: Genius Room screen status icons: Socket Server, Printer Queue, Messages
steps: Socket Server icon: shows the POS's current connection status with the socket server.
Printer Queue: opens a panel describing the printer's status.
Messages: opens the list of messages you have received.
entries.quote: Socket Server: This icon displays the current connection status of the POS with the socket server.

entries.title: Find a Genius device's name, IP address and app version
steps: Open Options > Settings > Info.
The Device section shows the device name, IP addresses and the POS app's version number.
The Communication section shows the network SSID, connected servers and network interfaces.
entries.quote: Device: Technical information about the POS device itself, such as its name, IP addresses, and the POS app’s version number.

entries.title: Attach a cash drawer before taking cash (iPad)
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right corner.
Tap Attach Drawer.
Enter the starting cash on the keypad if it is not preset.
Tap Confirm.
If you try a cash transaction with no drawer attached you get a message saying one needs to be attached.
entries.quote: they will receive a message stating it needs to be attached
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Connect an iPad to its card terminal or card reader
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right, then Manager, then Payment Terminals.
Tap the terminal. The iPad tries to connect to the PAX device.
Tap the Card Reader icon. If it worked the screen shows CONNECTED.
A magnetic stripe reader plugs into the iPad's headphone jack; a message says a reader was attached.
entries.quote: Tap to select one and it will attempt to connect to the PAX device.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Take a card payment on the Genius iPad app
steps: Open the ticket and tap Checkout.
For the full amount, swipe or dip the card while on the Checkout screen.
For a partial payment, enter the amount on the keypad first, then swipe the card.
To key in a card number, select Card and fill in the fields.
On approval choose Sign, Tip, Email, Print or Void Payment.
entries.quote: To take a credit payment for the full amount, swipe or dip the card while in the Checkout screen.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Void or change a payment taken today (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket.
At the bottom of the Ticket Preview, tap the payment.
Choose to change, print or void the payment. Void Payment asks for a void reason.
entries.quote: tap on the desired payment and you can change, print or void the payment
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: A payment from a previous day needs changing
steps: You cannot adjust transactions from previous days. You can only view and print them.
Tap the User Menu, then Reports, then Transactions, pick the date and tap Run.
Tap the ticket number, then View Original, to see and print the transaction.
To give money back, go to the Ticket Info screen and select Refund Ticket.
entries.quote: You cannot make adjustments to transactions from previous days, but you can view and print them.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Reprint a customer receipt or kitchen slip (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket and select Reprint from the left-hand menu.
Choose to reprint the customer receipt or a slip for the kitchen.
Use Preview to see the ticket in each format first.
entries.quote: From here you can reprint a Customer Receipt or reprint a slip to the kitchen
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Close a ticket by hand (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket once payment is final.
Select Close in the left-hand menu.
entries.quote: To close a ticket manually, go to the ticket and select Close in the left-hand menu.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Split a check on Genius (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket and select Split from the left-hand menu.
New creates an empty second check. Select items and use Move, or tap Check 1 or Check 2, to move them.
Evenly splits selected items evenly. Advanced splits an item into halves, thirds, quarters or fifths.
By Seat splits by seat. 2x to 9x splits everything evenly across that many checks.
Remove All undoes the splits.
entries.quote: Remove All – Selecting this will remove any previous splits
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Start and end a staff break (iPad)
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right and select Clock-Out.
Select Start Break, and the break type if asked. You are logged out.
When you return, log in and select End Break.
entries.quote: To go on break, select Start Break.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Message that you cannot check out until tickets are paid and closed
steps: A server or cash drawer checkout needs every ticket under that staff member closed and paid.
Close or transfer the open tickets.
Then select the User menu, Server Bank, and Checkout.
entries.quote: you’ll get a message advising that you cannot Checkout until the tickets are paid and closed
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: After a cash drawer checkout the drawer is detached
steps: Checking out a cash drawer detaches it from the iPad.
Attach a new drawer before taking more cash on that iPad.
entries.quote: A new drawer will need to be attached before taking additional cash transactions on that iPad.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Counting the cash drawer at checkout (Actual Cash Counting)
steps: If cash counting is on, checkout asks how much cash is in the drawer.
Enter the amount and select Save, or select Count Later.
If you choose Count Later, only someone with access to Daily Review can enter the count.
With this option on, every cash drawer must be counted to close the day properly.
entries.quote: If this option is checked, all cash drawers must be counted to close the day properly.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Reading the Daily Review marks at closing time (iPad)
steps: At closing you want a green checkmark or no indicator on Tips, Tickets and Cash.
A red X means that section still has items to complete.
entries.quote: Typically at closing time, you’ll want to see a green checkmark or no indicator for Tips, Tickets, and Cash.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: How to tell a Genius POS is offline (Cloud Sync icon, No Wi-Fi watermark)
steps: Look at the Cloud Sync icon at the top of the screen. A red badge with a number means the tablet is not communicating with the cloud.
The No Wi-Fi watermark means the iPad is not connected to the proper local network. It does not necessarily mean the internet is down.
entries.quote: If the connection is lost, the POS displays the icon with a red badge and a number in its corner.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: What does not work on Genius without internet
steps: Reports and time punch management need internet, because reports come from the cloud.
You cannot change your PIN without an internet connection.
Kiosk and Guest App orders need internet.
A guest display keeps working, but needs internet for its first login.
entries.quote: You cannot change your PIN number in the POS without an active internet connection.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Internet is down and cards will not process: Force Offline Credit Card Processing
steps: This only works if Offline Transactions was enabled for the location in the Admin Console beforehand, and with a magnetic stripe reader on the Monetary or BridgePay gateway.
In the POS tap the menu in the top right corner, then Manager, then General.
Turn on Force Offline Credit Card Processing. A yellow icon shows in the top panel.
Open the ticket, tap Checkout, and swipe the card on the magnetic stripe reader or enter the number by hand. With EMV terminals you may need to detach them to key in cards.
The ticket is marked Offline and shows purple.
When the internet is back, tap the yellow icon, tap Touch to show in Settings, and turn Force Offline Credit Card Processing off.
Risk: cards are not authorized while offline, so a card that later declines means the ticket is not paid.
entries.quote: In the General Settings screen, enable the Force Offline Credit Card Processing setting.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.
entries.not_ours: network not used by Processor Freedom (RS2 / BridgePay)

entries.title: Offline mode is not available when the internet drops
steps: Offline card processing must be switched on for the location before an outage.
In the Admin Console open Location Setup, tick Offline Transactions in the Transaction Settings area, click Save, then Publish.
If this was not enabled when the location went offline, staff cannot use offline mode.
entries.quote: If this setting is not enabled when a location goes offline, staff will be unable to use offline mode.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Authorize offline card payments once the internet is back
steps: In the POS tap the menu in the top right corner, then Manager, then Daily Review.
Tap Tickets, then Authorize All.
For pending tips tap Tips, then Capture Tips.
To do one ticket: open it, tap the Payment box near the bottom and tap Auth.
If a card is declined at this point it is likely an invalid card.
entries.quote: Tap Authorize All to authorize all the tickets with pending authorizations.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Store and Forward: what the red status bar and purple tickets mean
steps: If the site loses its connection, the POS shows a red status bar with a count of stored transactions waiting for approval.
While offline all card transactions are approved in offline mode and stored in a queue.
Tickets not yet authorized show purple and stay open, including through end of day, until they authorize.
When the connection returns the devices upload the stored transactions automatically. There is no way to authorize them by hand.
entries.quote: The status bar will also display a count of the number of stored transactions pending approval.

entries.title: Back online but offline (Store and Forward) payments have not authorized
steps: This is expected: once the site is back online, stored transactions can take from 2 to 24 hours to authorize.
Keep all devices connected to the POS, powered and online so every pending transaction uploads.
entries.quote: Once the site is back online, transactions can take from 2 to 24 hours to authorize.

entries.title: Store and Forward with the Reader: what it cannot do offline
steps: Not supported offline: bar tabs, gift cards, partial refunds, tip refunds, duplicate checking and reference refunds.
The merchant accepts the risk of loss: there is no guarantee a stored transaction will be approved.
entries.quote: At this time, Store and Forward does not support the following features or transaction types:

entries.title: Bad Debt on the Daily Summary Report (offline card payments that were declined)
steps: If an offline (Store and Forward) card payment is only partly approved later, the unapproved amount is reported as bad debt.
Transactions that are fully declined are also reported as Bad Debt.
It appears in the Transactions section of the Daily Summary Report.
entries.quote: Transactions that are fully declined will also be reported as “Bad Debt.”

entries.title: Switch a PAX Store and Forward site into offline mode by hand
steps: Store and Forward must already be boarded and set up for the site.
In the POS tap the menu in the top right corner, tap Manager, then General.
Turn on Force Offline Credit Card Processing.
Genius approves all transactions offline and queues them. It does not try to upload them until you turn the setting off again.
The ceiling limit still applies.
entries.quote: The program will not attempt to upload them again until you disable the offline mode.

entries.title: How long Genius can run offline and what keeps working
steps: It can run offline indefinitely. Orders are cached until the connection returns.
Printing, KDS and syncing between local devices keep working.
Online ordering, Kiosk, Guest App, reports, and card transactions (unless offline transactions are enabled) do not.
entries.quote: Printing, KDS, and local synchronization will be okay while
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Internet down: EMV payment terminals stop, a magnetic stripe reader can be the backup
steps: All LAN printers and KDS keep working, but EMV payment terminals are down.
Offline EMV transactions are not supported (per the 2020 FAQ).
A magnetic stripe reader on a supported gateway supports offline transactions and can be set up as a backup.
entries.quote: All LAN Printers and KDS will function but any Payment Terminals(EMV) will be down.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product. Newer Store and Forward guides describe offline card acceptance on the Reader and PAX devices.

entries.title: Sync In Progress
steps: The iPad is in the middle of syncing to the cloud. Syncing normally happens every 60 seconds.
If the message keeps appearing for a long time, an internet connection problem may be stopping the sync.
Restore the connection. Once syncing completes you can view and edit tickets again.
entries.quote: This message is showing because the iPad is in the middle of syncing up to the cloud.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Not on Wifi/Ethernet or No Sockets watermark on the Genius screen
steps: The no-Wi-Fi watermark means the device is offline. Get the connection back and it disappears.
The No Sockets watermark means printing is currently down.
In a special case it can be hidden: iPad Settings > Heartland Restaurant app > turn on Ignore Wifi Restrictions, then restart the app.
entries.quote: indicating that printing is currently down
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: You’re already attached to a drawer on another device
steps: You already have a drawer attached somewhere else.
Close any tickets open under that staff member.
Go to User Menu > Manager > Daily Review > Cash, tap the person icon on the open drawer, scroll to the bottom of the checkout and force a checkout.
If several people share the drawer, all of them need to be checked out.
entries.quote: if you already have a drawer attached somewhere else you will get this message
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: DEMO shows at the top right of a live Genius system
steps: It means the account is a demo account. A live account should never show it.
Contact support so the account can be corrected.
entries.quote: Live accounts should not show this at any time.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: A manager cannot see reports in the Genius app
steps: Most often it is the Report Access permission. In the Admin Portal check the staff member is assigned to a Report Access option with the needed reports ticked.
Three reports only exist in the Admin Portal: Dashboard, Ingredients and Loyalty.
More rarely, the site's firewall is blocking traffic.
entries.quote: This is most commonly due to permissions in Report Access.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Scan to Pay shows Unable to Fetch Ticket
steps: Check Scan to Pay is enabled under Location Setup > Rooms > QR Code.
Make sure the socket server tablet is connected to the internet.
Make sure the ticket's preview is not open in the system when the customer pays.
entries.quote: ensure that the socket server tablet is connected to the
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: If a Genius tablet dies, are its transactions lost?
steps: If the device had synced to the cloud and to the other tablets, the data is there.
If it failed before it could sync, those transactions or tickets may be overwritten or lost.
entries.quote: As long as the device synced its data to the cloud and locally to other tablets it will be there.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Refund a specific ticket (iPad, 2020 FAQ)
steps: Select the ticket.
Select Info from the left-hand menu and, under Ticket Actions, select Refund Ticket.
Confirm, then enter a reason for the refund.
Pay out the negative amount to the payment type you want.
entries.quote: A confirmation will appear to ensure you want to refund the ticket.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Where yesterday's closed tickets went
steps: Closed tickets are removed from the POS app at the configured End of Day.
They can still be viewed, reported on and reprinted in the Admin Portal under Reports, or in the POS app under User Menu > Reports.
entries.quote: are removed from the POS App at the configured
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Transfer a ticket to another staff member (iPad)
steps: Select the ticket.
Select Info from the left-hand menu.
Under Room/Owner tap Server and select the staff member.
Select Send from the left-hand menu to complete the transfer. Exit discards the change.
Whether you can transfer depends on the job type and the Modify Server permission.
entries.quote: it will discard this change and
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Keying in a card by hand fails because CVV is required
steps: On the Monetary gateway the CVV requirement on the manual entry form cannot be removed.
The processor may be able to adjust a setting to allow the transactions to be keyed. Contact the processor.
On PAX with Heartland a setting under Card Type can allow manual entry without CVV; that is a configuration change.
entries.quote: Therefore the CVV requirement cannot be removed.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Card terminal is stuck and the POS says a transaction is in progress
steps: Cancel on the card terminal itself first.
Only use the Cancel button on the POS (shown when a transaction takes longer than 30 seconds) if the terminal does not report that it cancelled.
Cancelling on the POS does not guarantee the terminal stops trying to process, especially when the two have lost their connection.
If the Cancel button setting is disabled, the POS waits 5 minutes for the terminal before letting you do anything else.
entries.quote: We always advise cancelling from the EMV device itself first

entries.title: A payment void failed and the POS offers a Force void
steps: A Force void is not sent to the processor at all. It only removes the transaction from Genius reporting.
If you force void, write down the transaction details.
Contact the processor so the transaction is handled on their side.
Global Payments recommends keeping the Force Voids setting off except for one-off needs.
entries.quote: A Force void is not communicated to the processor whatsoever

entries.title: Cannot open a ticket because it is being changed on another station
steps: With Ticket Locking on, a ticket being viewed or changed on another device is locked and the message cannot be bypassed.
Close the ticket on the other station, then open it again.
entries.quote: it will give a message that cannot be bypassed

entries.title: Firewall blocking Genius: domains to allow
steps: If the site has a firewall, the Global Payments article lists the domains to allow, including *.heartland.us, *.appcenter.ms, *.eloview.com, *.datadoghq.com and *.gpapis.globalpay.com.
With EMV terminals a more detailed list is provided, because those terminals talk directly to the processor.
Give the article to whoever manages the network.
entries.quote: *.gpapis.globalpay.com (ports 443, 8002, 8080, 8081)

entries.title: ControlScan-managed Genius networks: changes go through ControlScan
steps: If the site's network is managed by ControlScan, any change has to go through ControlScan.
The article gives the ControlScan support number as (800) 393-3246, option 1.
entries.quote: Any changes with ControlScan has to go though control scan.

entries.title: Genius Admin Portal: Troubleshoot and Request Screenshot for a device
steps: In the Admin Portal open the Authorized Devices screen and click Troubleshoot on the device.
The panel shows diagnostic counts such as items waiting to upload.
Click Request Screenshot to have the device send a screenshot of the POS app; click Refresh until it appears.
Remove deletes a device so another permanent device can be added within the licence limit.
entries.quote: If you click Request Screenshot, the selected device will take a screenshot of its own screen

entries.title: Load receipt paper in the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Lift the top lid of the printer to loosen the cover.
Tilt the cover back to expose the paper roll.
Place the roll in the device with the paper feeding from the bottom.
Close the printer cover.
entries.quote: Loosen the cover by lifting the top lid of the printer.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Charge the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Plug the USB-A end of the cable into the power supply and the USB-C end into the charging base, then plug the supply into an outlet.
Place the device in the base, leading with the bottom lip of the device.
The device beeps to confirm it is charging.
entries.quote: the Mobile Point of Sale device will beep to confirm it is charging
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Turn on the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Press and hold the power button on the left side until the screen powers on.
Release it when the orange boot logo appears.
entries.quote: Release the button once the orange boot logo appears.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Connect the Mobile 2.0 handheld to Wi-Fi
steps: With the device on, swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap and hold the Network icon until a password prompt appears.
Enter the password given in the guide: Global99.
Select your Wi-Fi network, enter its password and tap Connect.
The handheld and the other point-of-sale equipment must be on the same network.
entries.quote: Please verify that both the Handheld POS device and other point-of-sale equipment are on the same network.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 handheld is showing the End of Day screen
steps: Swipe up on the device and tap the app overview button.
Tap the Genius tile. The Genius app comes back to the front.
entries.quote: The Mobile 2.0 device is displaying the “End of Day” screen.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 handheld cannot take a payment
steps: Check the Payments and PA apps are both running in the background. Their icons show in the notification bar at the top; if not, open the Apps screen and run the Payments app.
Check the device is connected to the location's Wi-Fi.
Check the battery is at least 10% charged. Below 10% the Payments app will not work. Put the device on the charger and charge above 25%.
entries.quote: If its battery drops below 10%, the Payments app will not function.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0: the battery pack cannot be swapped
steps: If the battery is low, put the handheld on the charger and charge above 25%.
The battery pack cannot be swapped out.
entries.quote: Place the Mobile 2.0 device on the charger and charge above 25%.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Genius app shows a red icon in the top panel (handheld not connected to the socket server)
steps: The red icon means the device is not connected to the Dedicated Socket Server.
Check the handheld is on the same Wi-Fi network as the Dedicated Socket Server.
Check the Dedicated Socket Server device is running the Genius app and is on that same network.
entries.quote: the device is not connected to the Dedicated Socket Server
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 app is not updating to the latest version
steps: Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and open the app overview.
Swipe the Genius tile up to close it.
Open the Apps screen and tap the Genius icon. This starts a version check and update.
A blank white screen means the app is checking for and installing the latest version. Make sure the device is on the location's Wi-Fi.
entries.quote: This will initiate a JS Version check and update.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Network Unplugged/Terminal IP No Connection Error
steps: The device is not connected to the network, or the Downloader could not download an update.
Check the device is connected to the network and try the download again.
If it is on the right network and the error stays: swipe down from the top and tap the Settings icon. The guide gives the password Global99.
Tap Wi-Fi, tap and hold the current network and tap Forget Network.
Reboot the device, open Settings and connect to the network again.
Run the Downloader app again.
entries.quote: Network Unplugged/Terminal IP No Connection Error
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Download Error Terminal Code: 300 Cannot Connect
steps: Same cause and fix as Network Unplugged: the device is not on the network, or the Downloader failed to fetch an update.
Check the network connection and try the download again.
If it persists, forget the Wi-Fi network in Settings, reboot, reconnect and run the Downloader app again.
entries.quote: or Download Error Terminal Code: 300 Cannot Connect
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: D2 RETRY LATER - The transaction cannot be completed at this time. Retry later.
steps: This is a response from the card issuer, the bank or card company behind the card.
Ask the customer to try a different card.
entries.quote: This is a card issuer response.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Keys Not Injected
steps: The device cannot be used until its keys are re-injected.
It has to be sent back to the hardware team for that.
entries.quote: This will require the device to be sent back to the hardware team to reinject.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 POS app is frozen: close and relaunch it
steps: Swipe up from the bottom of the screen.
Tap the Overview button.
Press the POS app's tile and swipe it up until it disappears.
Open the Apps screen and launch the POS app again.
entries.quote: Press the POS app’s tile and swipe up until it disappears from the screen.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 shows a Please Wait screen after restarting
steps: This is normal: the Payments app starts by itself after a restart and shows Please Wait because it is meant to keep running in the background.
Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and tap the Home button.
On the Home screen, run the Restaurant POS app.
entries.quote: the Payments app automatically runs and displays the “Please Wait” screen
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0: clear the POS app's data (last resort)
steps: In the POS Tickets screen tap Options, then System Logout.
Swipe down from the top, tap Settings and enter a valid password.
Tap Apps, then the Restaurant icon, then Storage.
Tap Clear Data and OK, then Clear Cache.
Reboot the device and run the POS app.
You will need a valid Device Login Code to sign back in, so have one ready before you start.
entries.quote: The Restaurant POS app will display a prompt for a Device Login Code.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Things the Mobile 2.0 handheld cannot do (use the iPad POS instead)
steps: The guide lists: referenced refunds, server checkouts, clock ins, Scan to Pay transactions, item discounts, advanced item splits, and duplicate ingredients and sub-items.
entries.quote: For what features should I continue to use the iOS POS?
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: WiseCube card reader is not connecting
steps: Charge the reader first if it is not charged.
Plug the power cord into the Mobile POS enclosure to wake the reader, wait ten seconds, and tap the card icon at the top of the POS to see if it is connected.
On the iPad open Settings > Bluetooth and check the reader is connected. If not, tap the CHBxxxx device to connect, then reopen the app.

If that fails: close the app, tap the Information button for the WiseCube in the Bluetooth list and tap Forget device. Reopen the app, go to Settings > Manager > Payment Terminals, tap Scan for WiseCube Devices and tap Pair.

Last resort: remove the reader from the enclosure, hold its power button until it powers off, turn the iPad's Bluetooth off and on, turn the reader back on (its lights chase), then scan and pair again.
entries.quote: Tap Scan for WiseCube Devices.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Error System Error (WiseCube)
steps: Either CrossTID is not enabled on the processing file, or the processing URL used for WiseCube devices is down.
Call processing to re-enable CrossTID for the WiseCube device, or to report or confirm the outage.
If it is an outage, wait for processing to be restored.
entries.quote: CrossTID is not enabled on the processing file.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Error Offlinedecline (WiseCube)
steps: The device is misconfigured.
It needs to be returned and replaced (an RMA).
entries.quote: The device is misconfigured and needs an RMA.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Insert, swipe, or try another card error (WiseCube)
steps: The card may have been inserted the wrong way. Flip it over and try again.
The card may be defective. Try another card.
entries.quote: The card was inserted incorrectly; flip the card over and try again.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Tap does not work on the Mobile POS (WiseCube)
steps: The reader is not installed correctly in the enclosure.
Refit it so the NFC logo on the reader faces the NFC logo on the enclosure.
entries.quote: The EMV device needs to have the NFC logo facing to the NFC logo on the enclosure.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: WiseCube Error
steps: Restart the tablet and the WiseCube device.
If failures continue, uninstall and reinstall the Heartland Restaurant POS application.
entries.quote: Attempt to restart the tablet and the WiseCube device.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Frequent WiseCube disconnections in the MobilePOS case: battery removal
steps: Global Payments saw far fewer disconnections between the iPad Mini and the WiseCube once the HBSM-CH60 battery was removed from the case.
Removing it means opening the case with tools and can cause irreparable damage, so this is not a job for the merchant.
After removal the case needs charging after each busy shift.
entries.quote: we have seen a significant decrease in disconnections between the iPad Mini and BBPOS Wisecube when this battery has been removed
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Staff swipe card is not recognised, or the POS keeps showing Swipe Card to Link
steps: The swipe was probably unreadable: misaligned, too fast or too slow.
Swipe again with a steady motion, with the magnetic stripe facing the right way (usually shown by the light on the Reader).
Check the stripe is clean and intact. Debris, sticky residue or deep scratches can stop it reading.
entries.quote: Cause: The swipe was likely unreadable, for some reason (misaligned, too fast, or too slow).

entries.title: Assign a swipe card to a staff member on Genius
steps: Log in to a POS device that is connected to the internet, with an account allowed to assign PINs and cards.
Open the User Menu and tap Assign Card.
Select the staff member.
Swipe an unassigned card through the reader at a steady, moderate speed.
The POS shows a confirmation message.
entries.quote: Access the User Menu, then tap Assign Card.

entries.title: XC23 camera: features missing, blank or blurry picture, slow scanning
steps: Features missing: connect the camera as in the setup steps and reboot the POS terminal.
Blank or blurry: check the lens for obstructions and remove any plastic film. If it continues, reboot the POS terminal.
Slow or failed scanning: make sure the area has enough light.
entries.quote: Remove any plastic film that may be covering the lens.

entries.title: Pair the Zebra DS2278 Bluetooth scanner with a Genius iPad
steps: Scan the two programming barcodes shown in the Global Payments article.
Press the button on the scanner to begin pairing.
On the tablet open Bluetooth settings and make sure Bluetooth is on.
Tap the device named DS2278 followed by numbers and check it shows Connected.
entries.quote: press the button on the scanner to begin pairing with the tablet or computer

entries.title: Barcode scanner does not scan when picked up off its stand
steps: It does not scan automatically when picked up.
Press the black button on top to scan while holding it.
entries.quote: to scan while picked up you must press the black button on top

entries.title: Caller ID box is not sending calls to Genius
steps: Make sure Multicast is enabled on the network and port 4100 is open.
Make sure port 3520 is open for UDP traffic.
The box must be on the same local network as the tablets.
A ticket must be open on the Ticket Info screen to receive the call.
Only the supported Whozz Calling boxes work; Deluxe boxes do not. For phone-line wiring or dip switches contact Whozz Calling.
entries.quote: Ensure a ticket is open and on the Ticket Info screen to receive the call.

entries.title: Wire a Genius iPad stand to Ethernet (Ethernet cable kit)
steps: Plug the Ethernet adapter into the internal cable of the Genius stand.
Plug the Lightning end of the Y cable into the Ethernet adapter.
Plug the male USB-A end of the Y cable into the Apple power brick.
Plug in an Ethernet cable.
Connect the Apple power brick to a power source.
Newer iPads use USB-C instead of Lightning; the cabling is otherwise identical.
entries.quote: Plug the ethernet adapter into the internal cable of the Genius stand.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: HotSauce Support: phone option and email
steps: Call HotSauce Support on 678.325.5300 and choose option 2.
Or email support@hotsaucepos.com.
HotSauce's FAQ describes the support department as 24/7.
entries.quote: HotSauce Support 678.325.5300 opt #2 support@hotsaucepos.com

entries.title: What must be ready on site before a HotSauce installation
steps: The counter or desktop is installed where the terminal will go, with a hole of at least 1-1/2 inches for cables if needed.
Powered electrical outlets are within 5 feet of the computer's location.
The DSL or cable modem is installed and the internet is working.
All network wiring (CAT 5 / Ethernet) is run and terminated. HotSauce does not run Ethernet cabling; it recommends a local company.
Remote printer wiring is run and terminated.
entries.quote: Hostsauce does not and cannot run ethernet cabling.

entries.title: When HotSauce installations happen and who does them
steps: Installations are only performed Monday to Thursday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Eastern.
HotSauce contracts a local installation tech to install the POS hardware on site, supported remotely by the HotSauce implementation team.
That visit covers HotSauce hardware only: not wiring, third party equipment or on-site training.
entries.quote: Any and all installations are only performed/completed: Monday - Thursday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Eastern

entries.title: HotSauce Go Live call: what gets checked on the first day
steps: The HotSauce implementation team contacts the merchant on the first day of live use, ideally 1 to 2 hours before opening.
Together you run through order placement, processing a credit card, the cash drawer opening, all printers, and the end of shift and end of day procedure.
A follow-up call happens 3 to 5 days after Go Live.
entries.quote: Order Placement, Processing Credit Card, Cash Drawer Opens, All Printers Work, End of Shift and End of Day Procedure

entries.title: How HotSauce staff training is delivered
steps: Training is by online video, in English and Spanish. HotSauce provides the video links.
On-site training is available for an additional fee.
entries.quote: HotSauce POS Training is done via online video.

entries.title: HotSauce menu review before install
steps: The implementation team reviews the whole configured menu with the merchant: items, modifiers and pricing.
Have a computer or laptop and the day-to-day manager on the call.
Skipping the review leads to problems using the system.
entries.quote: Items, Modifiers and Pricing will be reviewed.

entries.title: HotSauce preferred hardware (which printer, drawer and terminal models to expect)
steps: POS terminal: Partnertech Grace G4 or SP550 touch POS system.
Receipt (thermal) printer: Partnertech RP-630.
Kitchen (dot matrix) printer: SNBC M-300 or Epson TM-U220B.
Cash drawer: Partnertech CDR-6E410. Barcode scanner: Honeywell 1250G-2USB. Scale: Avery Berkel 6712.
Routers: MikroTik hEX RB750Gr3 or RB760iGS, or TP-Link ER605. Wireless access point: TP-Link EAP225 V3 or Ubiquiti UniFi AP AC.
Kitchen display: Logic Control LS8900 with KB9000 bump bar.
entries.quote: HOTSAUCE POS PREFERRED HARDWARE LIST

entries.title: HotSauce needs a Gigabit network switch
steps: Use a Gigabit switch (up to 1000 Mbps).
So-called Fast switches max out at 100 Mbps and are too slow.
entries.quote: "Fast" switches are too slow, and max out at 100 Mbps.
